purpose: Independent references for actual White opening/setup and Black response; no copying of commentary into product

sources.observed: 1.Nf3 is called Reti on Chess.com. Later c4 or d4 can change family; Nf3 c5 e4 reaches Sicilian.
Black chooses Sicilian with e4 c5. The line e4 c5 Nf3 e6 remains Sicilian, French Variation. Alapin is White's c3 choice.
White starts with c4. Black e5 gives Reversed Sicilian; c5 gives Symmetrical English. These are not the same as Black answering e4 with a Sicilian.
e4 e6 is French Defense; the response is already named before d4 d5.
e4 c6 is Caro-Kann; d4 d5 is a common continuation, not required to identify the initial response.
Chess.com gives e4 d6 as the Pirc start, with d4 Nf6 Nc3 g6 as the main line.
cases: e4 d6 d4 Nf6 Nc3 g6

sources.observed: Chess.com's starting position is d4 Nf6 c4 g6. Black's g6 alone is not enough without White's central choice.
d4 Nf6 c4 g6 Nc3 d5 is Grunfeld, a new classification after Black d5.
cases: d4 Nf6 c4 g6 Nc3 d5

sources.observed: Nimzo-Indian needs the actual line d4 Nf6 c4 e6 Nc3 Bb4. Do not classify at the shared e6 prefix.
cases: d4 Nf6 c4 e6 Nc3 Bb4

sources.observed: White's c4 offer follows d4 d5. Black c6, e6, and dxc4 distinguish Slav, Declined, and Accepted respectively.
White chooses the Ruy Lopez at e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5; a Black variation cannot be inferred before its defining reply.
Black a6 after the Ruy Lopez confirms Morphy Defense.
cases: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6

sources.observed: Black Nf6 after the Ruy Lopez confirms Berlin Defense.
cases: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 Nf6

sources.observed: White chooses the Italian with Bc4 after e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6. Black Bc5 confirms Giuoco Piano.
cases: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Bc5

sources.observed: Black Nf6 responds to the Italian as Two Knights Defense.
cases: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Nf6

sources.observed: White Bf4 before e3 defines the London setup. The d4 Nf6 Bf4 g6 line is described as London's Indian setup; it need not be called King's Indian Defense.
The official root page shows d4 d6 c4 g6 as Modern Defense.
Portuguese Opening is White's Bb5 choice in e4 e5 Bb5, not a Black defense.
An aggregated set of names with representative PGN move orders and position EPD; not a complete theory, win-rate, or independent white/black-opening database.

interpretation: Side labels are authored presentation of one shared opening, not evidence that two independent opening names must always exist.
The existing matcher already prefers exact history over transposition for current names. No unsupported claim of a general matching defect.
Positive line cases and forbidden premature labels are chosen from the sources before examining the new classifier.
A position-only custom FEN cannot establish the player's original first-move choice. Last-known names must remain visibly historical.
